dedupe_keys.name: silver strategic integration of large capacity variable energy resources electricity dispatch model

description: SILVER (Strategic Integration of Large-capacity Variable Energy Resources) is a scenario-based electricity system model from the SESIT group at the University of Victoria. The G-PST Open Tools Portal says it explores trade-offs among balancing strategies for grids with high shares of variable renewable energy, optimising asset dispatch for a user-defined system that specifies demand response availability, generation, storage and transmission. The README describes a generic, object-oriented Python network optimisation tool, tested with Python 3.9.16, split into four stages: input processing, a price-setting optimal power flow, unit commitment and a real-time optimal power flow; the last three loop over each commitment period in the chosen time range, with linear programmes solved for each hour. Coverage: any user-defined electricity system; example inputs for one scenario ship with the repository. Format and access: Python source on GitLab (sesit/silver) with a user manual PDF in the repository; the repository showed activity on 28 September 2026. Licence: MIT (portal). Caveats: the user manual was not read, and the solver requirements are not stated in the README. Simulation uses: hourly dispatch, unit commitment and power flow studies for systems with high wind and solar shares, including storage and demand response. Related records: COPPER (model-copper-canadian-electricity-capacity-expansion) plans capacity for the same group's Canadian studies, and IDEA (platform-idea-energy-transition-dashboard) visualises SILVER outputs.
